mappings.note: The Sanjan legend of sugar dissolved in milk without spilling, read as a promise of enrichment without disruption. CG-SST2 for the founding story of the Parsi settlement, LO-83 for the inclusion it stands for - the frame's nearest outcome, since it has none for civilisational pluralism as such.

Tracing on a world map the sea and land routes the Jews, Parsis, Armenians, Syriac Christians and Tibetans took, and the terrain each crossed. Map and terrain work; goal-level CG-SST1, LO-73 being climatic regions only.

The values that let India absorb newcomers - vasudhaiva kutumbakam, atithi devo bhava, ahimsa, karuna. LO-83 as the nearest real outcome, equality and inclusion in public life; the frame has no outcome for civilisational values, which is the gap here.

Parsis such as Homi Bhabha and Ratan Tata, and the task of finding contributors from other communities. Goal-level CG-SST4 for its clause on recognising the contributions of different sections of society - the one place this frame reaches such a question.
A group project researching each settled community. Historical study of migration and settlement, goal-level CG-SST2. (The stored answer belongs to the Travancore Torah-crown question; see report.)
Reading a 19th-century photograph of a Mumbai Jewish family in Indian dress for evidence of integration. Inference from a visual source, goal-level CG-SST2.
A Syriac Christian wedding combining Christian rite with silk saree and mangalsutra. Visual evidence of cultural fusion, goal-level CG-SST2.
Ravi Varma's Parsi bride in a regionally draped saree with Indian jewellery. Visual evidence of integration, goal-level CG-SST2.

The Maharaja of Travancore's gold crown for the Kochi synagogue's Torah in 1805. CG-SST2 for the historical act and its evidence, LO-83 for the protection and equal standing it signalled to a minority.
Siddi dancers of African descent in sarees, nose rings and bangles. Visual evidence of fusion, goal-level CG-SST2.

Identifying long-settled communities in one's own neighbourhood and discussing their experience. LO-85 is a genuine fit - interpreting social issues in one's own region - with CG-SST2 for the migration history behind them.

Collecting local stories that carry the same values of welcome, such as Krishna and Sudama. LO-83 for equality and acceptance; LO-82 is rejected outright, being bhakti and sufi poetry read for social order.

Arguing both sides of sheltering a stranger, then extending it to refugees reaching India. LO-83 for the principle of equal treatment, LO-85 because the task asks students to apply it to a live public issue.
Defines the chapter's subject - communities that fled persecution abroad and settled permanently in India. Historical migration, goal-level CG-SST2.
Defines a synagogue as the Jewish place of worship. LO-80 covers places of worship and their construction, and is the only outcome in this frame that reaches one.
Baha'u'llah as founder of the Baha'i faith. The emergence of a new religious movement, LO-81 exactly.
Syriac Christians persecuted because their teaching on the nature of Christ diverged from official doctrine. Doctrinal difference producing a distinct religious community, LO-81.

AYUSH as the government framework for Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Sowa Rigpa and Homoeopathy. A government institution; goal-level CG-SST4, since C-SST4.2's LOs are a local market visit and a State office report.
Raja Jadi Rana of Sanjan granting the fleeing Zoroastrians a home. Historical act of settlement, goal-level CG-SST2.

Armenian Street and St Mary's Armenian Church in Chennai as a community's surviving footprint. Goal-level CG-SST2; LO-80 is rejected because the church is named as a landmark, not described as architecture.

Defines persecution as systematic hostility on religious, ethnic or political grounds. Persecution is the negation of equal standing, so LO-83 is the nearest real outcome; LO-81 is rejected because no religious movement is being explained.
Men-Tsee-Khang in Dharamshala keeping Sowa Rigpa alive. An institution founded by a refugee community to preserve its tradition, goal-level CG-SST2.
Baha'is persecuted in Persia because their teaching of unity was branded heretical. The emergence of a new religious movement and the resistance to it, LO-81.
Digvijaysinhji of Nawanagar sheltering a thousand Polish orphans in the Second World War. CG-SST2 for the event, LO-83 for the principle of shelter extended regardless of origin.
Arabic filfil from Sanskrit pippali. Linguistic evidence of ancient trade contact, goal-level CG-SST2. (This cognate table belongs to Chapter 3, not to this chapter; see report.)

Why Siddis are a scheduled tribe - rich culture but poor economic condition, requiring affirmative action. LO-84 because the item turns on economic as distinct from social standing, LO-85 because it asks students to read a live equality issue.
Vasudhaiva kutumbakam, 'the whole world is family'. LO-83 as the nearest outcome for a value of inclusion; the frame has none for civilisational values.
Syriac Christians settling on the Malabar coast after fleeing Roman and Persian persecution. Migration history, goal-level CG-SST2; CG-SST1 is not added because the coast is named, not located.
Parsis fleeing after the 7th-century Arab conquest of the Sassanid empire. Migration history, goal-level CG-SST2.
Zarathushtra and Ahura Mazda. The founding of a religious tradition, LO-81.
The Mappila community and the Cheraman Juma Masjid, India's oldest mosque. LO-80 names mosques explicitly; CG-SST2 for the Arab settlement and intermarriage that produced the community.

Lady Juliana, Armenian physician at the Mughal court. Evidence of a community's standing; goal-level CG-SST2, and LO-89 is rejected because the item shows a woman's position rather than a disadvantage.
Indian expatriate communities seen as peaceful, integrating minorities that strengthen host economies. Contribution of a section of society, goal-level CG-SST4.
Old Avestan sharing roots and grammar with Vedic Sanskrit. Linguistic evidence of shared ancient heritage, goal-level CG-SST2.
Armenian merchants valued by the Mughals for commerce and for administrative, military and household service. A community's role in an earlier polity, goal-level CG-SST2.
The Udvada fire temple with its continuous flame, closed to outsiders. A place of worship and its practice, LO-80, the only outcome here reaching one.

The Karaniya Metta Sutta on cherishing all beings as a mother her child. LO-81 for the religious teaching, LO-83 for the universal regard it expresses; LO-82 is rejected, being specific to bhakti and sufi verse.
Bene Israel arriving around 175 BCE. Dating a migration, goal-level CG-SST2.
Jizya levied on Zoroastrians after the Arab conquest of Persia. A historical fiscal measure driving migration, goal-level CG-SST2.
Nalanda's recorded links with the Muara Jambi complex. Historical scholarly exchange, goal-level CG-SST2. (The answer itself notes this is carried over from an earlier chapter; see report.)
Identifying the Siddis from African drumming and dance fused with Gujarati speech and Indian religion. Migration and cultural fusion, goal-level CG-SST2.
The Red Cross as the Maharaja of Nawanagar's partner in rescuing Polish orphans, 1942-46. Historical event, goal-level CG-SST2.
The Raja of Kochi granting Jewish settlers land 'as long as the world, sun and moon endure'. CG-SST2 for the grant as historical fact, LO-83 for the standing it conferred on a minority.
Siddis originating in Africa and brought to India from the 7th century by Arab, Portuguese and British traders. Forced migration, goal-level CG-SST2.
Akbar permitting Armenians to build a church and practise in Agra. A ruler's grant to a settled minority, goal-level CG-SST2; LO-80 is rejected because the church is not described.

Vivekananda in 1893 on belonging to a nation that has sheltered the persecuted of all religions. LO-83 for the claim about equal shelter; CG-SST2 is not added because the quotation is used as a value statement rather than a source. (Stray option text is appended to the answer; see report.)
Jamnagar in Gujarat as where the Polish orphans were settled. Historical fact of refuge, goal-level CG-SST2.
Asuras as demonic in post-Vedic India but Ahura as the supreme good god in the Avesta. Divergence of two religious traditions from shared roots, LO-81.
Siddis blending African religious practice with Hinduism, Islam or Christianity. LO-81 for the religious syncretism, CG-SST2 for the cultural integration it evidences.
Sarve bhavantu sukhinah, 'may all creatures be happy'. LO-83 as the nearest outcome for a value of universal regard.
The Lotus Temple as the Baha'i house of worship in Delhi. A place of worship, LO-80; LO-81 is reserved for items about the faith's teachings or origin.
Tibet becoming a Buddhist centre in the 7th century when its king embraced the teachings. Spread of a religious movement, LO-81.

Dalai Lamas as Tibet's spiritual heads and rulers from the 15th century. A religious institution and its authority, LO-81; LO-78 is rejected because the frame's administrative outcome concerns Indian kingdoms of the period studied.
The 14th Dalai Lama fleeing Lhasa for India in 1959. A dated migration into India, goal-level CG-SST2, matching the other flight-and-refuge items.

The Dalai Lama's commitments - human values, religious harmony, Tibetan culture, and reviving karuna and ahimsa - against the false claim that he promotes conversion. LO-83 for the value strand, LO-81 for religious harmony between traditions. (Stem survives only as its last line; see report.)
Atithi devo bhava, 'a guest is like God'. LO-83 as the nearest outcome for the value of welcome.
The Baha'i faith originating in mid-1800s Persia, now Iran. The emergence of a religious movement, LO-81; the country is incidental, so CG-SST1 is not cited.
Sowa Rigpa as the Tibetan 'Art of Healing', blending Ayurveda with Chinese, Persian and Greek inputs. A knowledge tradition and its transmission, goal-level CG-SST2.
Bene Israel from the Kingdom of Israel, shipwrecked onto the Konkan coast. Migration history, goal-level CG-SST2.

Tibetan settlements in states such as Karnataka letting the community build monasteries and keep its language and faith alive. CG-SST2 for the refugee settlement, LO-83 because the point is a minority given space to remain itself on equal terms.
